name: Civil Network OPORA
tagline: We observe elections, monitor parliament, analyze social media data and the language of war, and collect information about Russian war crimes.
project_type: civic monitoring / election observation / think tank
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
team_size: large network (30,000+ observers, hundreds of long-term staff and regional coordinators)
dependency_risks: Russian full-scale invasion disrupting activities in occupied territories

news_articles.headline: Olga Aivazovska, Opora: Ukraine 'needs to strive for building strong legal institutions'
Ukrainian EPDE members CVU and Opora publish expert reports

policy_outcomes.description: Parallel vote tabulation across 23 electoral campaigns with zero discrepancies from official results
Co-founded the European Platform for Democratic Elections (EPDE), a network of nonpartisan election observers
Trained more than 70,000 police officers on electoral law and monitoring standards

outcome_methodology: Parallel Vote Tabulation (PVT) using statistically representative sample; long-term and short-term field observers; parliamentary vote monitoring
documented_limitations: elections currently suspended due to martial law
dependent on volunteer and donor-funded observer networks
jurisdictional_scope: national (Ukraine), with some international election observation experience
failure_modes: inability to operate in conflict zones
governance_model: independent civic network with board of directors; chairperson Olga Aivazovska
contributor_governance: regional coordinators and trained observer network; national and regional levels
political_bias_allegations: OPORA maintains explicitly non-partisan stance; no credible bias allegations found

government_partnerships.type: funded project on democratic integrity and governance

ai_involvement: Social media data analysis and language-of-war monitoring; no AI-specific tools confirmed
